vulnerabilities.title: Workshop management page accessible to any member
vulnerabilities.source: Any authenticated member can navigate to /workshops/manage
vulnerabilities.notes: The route uses @members_only but should use @staff_only. A normal member (bob) can GET /workshops/manage and see all workshops and all reservations including other members' data.

vulnerabilities.title: Booking receipt accessible without authentication
vulnerabilities.source: An unauthenticated visitor can navigate to /bookings/<rid>/receipt
vulnerabilities.notes: The receipt route has no @members_only decorator. Anyone, even without logging in, can access /bookings/1/receipt and see the member's name, email, booking details and cost.

vulnerabilities.title: Any member can view any other member's booking details
vulnerabilities.source: The rid path parameter selects any reservation regardless of owner
vulnerabilities.notes: The detail route fetches the reservation by id (WHERE r.id = ?) without checking that r.owner_id matches the logged-in account. Bob can view Alice's booking at /bookings/1.

vulnerabilities.title: Booking total cost accepted from client form instead of server calculation
vulnerabilities.source: The total_cost hidden form field in the booking form
vulnerabilities.notes: The server reads total_cost directly from the submitted form data instead of computing it as seats * price_per_seat. An attacker can submit total_cost=0 (or any value) to book seats for free.

vulnerabilities.title: No validation on seat count allows zero or negative bookings
vulnerabilities.source: The seats form field in the booking form
vulnerabilities.notes: The seat count is taken from the form with no range check. Submitting seats=-5 creates a reservation with negative seats. There is also no check against remaining capacity.

vulnerabilities.title: Profile update writes role and credit_balance from form data
vulnerabilities.source: Hidden or injected role and credit_balance form fields on POST /profile
vulnerabilities.notes: The update_profile handler reads role and credit_balance from the form and writes them to the database. The template only shows display_name and email inputs, but an attacker can add role=admin and credit_balance=99999 to the POST body to escalate privileges and set arbitrary credit.

vulnerabilities.title: Profile update form has no CSRF protection
vulnerabilities.source: A cross-site form submission to POST /profile
vulnerabilities.notes: The update_profile handler does not check a CSRF token, and the profile.html template does not include a _csrf hidden input. Other state-changing forms in the app (login, workshop create/edit, add note, admin update) all validate CSRF. A malicious page can submit a form to /profile on behalf of a logged-in user.

vulnerabilities.title: Any member can cancel any other member's booking
vulnerabilities.anchor: UPDATE reservations SET status = 'cancelled' WHERE id = ?
vulnerabilities.source: The rid path parameter in POST /bookings/<rid>/cancel
vulnerabilities.notes: The cancel route updates the reservation by id without checking that the logged-in user owns it. Bob can POST /bookings/1/cancel to cancel Alice's booking.

decoys.title: Workshop edit form is staff-only
decoys.why_safe: The edit_form and edit routes both have the @staff_only decorator (which itself wraps @members_only), so only staff and admin accounts can access workshop editing. A normal member gets redirected.

decoys.title: Booking list filters by owner_id
decoys.why_safe: The my_bookings route includes WHERE r.owner_id = ? with the logged-in account's id, so each member only sees their own bookings. Bob cannot see Alice's bookings in the listing.

decoys.title: Add-note route checks reservation ownership via helper
decoys.why_safe: The add_note route calls verify_reservation_owner() from db.py, which queries the database to confirm the reservation belongs to the logged-in user before allowing the note. Bob cannot add notes to Alice's bookings.

decoys.title: Admin member list has inline role check
decoys.why_safe: The admin_list and admin_detail routes use @members_only plus an inline check (if g.account['role'] != 'admin') that redirects non-admin users. The check is not in a decorator but is still effective. Bob (a member) gets redirected with a permission error.

decoys.title: Admin member update has both role check and CSRF validation
decoys.why_safe: The admin_update route checks the admin role inline and validates the CSRF token with valid_csrf(). The admin_member_detail.html template includes the _csrf hidden input. Both the access control and CSRF protections are present, unlike the profile update route.
